To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the measurement of central blood pressure, arterial wave reflection, and arterial stiffness is an important component of total cardiovascular risk assessment in hypertensive patients.

central blood pressure is a more reliable indicator of cardiovascular risk than peripheral blood pressure, and that the attenuation of central blood pressure, wave reflections, or arterial stiffness is a more powerful predictor of cardiovascular risk than the reduction of peripheral blood pressure.

central blood pressure is a better predictor of cardiovascular events than brachial blood pressure, that central blood pressure can be estimated noninvasively by means of pulse wave analysis, and that central blood pressure reduction is a new therapeutic target in essential hypertension, as shown by clinical trials with newer antihypertension agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evaluation of the relationship between arterial stiffness and wave reflections, central hemodynamics, and target organ damage in essential hypertension and with the effects of antihypertensives on these parameters.
the following questions: What is the role of central blood pressure, arterial wall stiffness, and wave reflections in the cardiovascular risk of patients with arterial hypertension?
the following questions: (1) What is the role of central arterial stiffness and wave reflections in the development of target organ disease?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

arterial stiffness and central blood pressure should be considered as important components for the assessment of total cardiovascular risk, and that newer antihypertensives may have a greater protective effect on cardiovascular events than older drugs, independent of peripheral blood pressures.

central blood pressure and arterial stiffness should be evaluated in patients with high cardiovascular risk, and that newer drugs that are effective in reducing central blood pressure and improving arterial stiffness should be preferred in the treatment of hypertension.
arterial stiffness and wave reflection are independent predictors of cardiovascular events and that the attenuation of these parameters may be a useful therapeutic target in hypertensive patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arterial stiffness is an important determinant of cardiovascular risk, and its measurement should be included in routine clinical practice.
the evaluation of arterial stiffness and central blood pressure may be useful in selected patients to better identify those at risk of developing target organ damage.
central blood pressure and arterial stiffness are important new markers of cardiovascular risk in hypertensive patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evaluation of central hemodynamics and arterial stiffness may help us better understand the pathophysiology of hypertension and may be used as a tool to better assess the cardiovascular risk of patients and their response to therapy.
arterial stiffness and wave reflection are important determinants of central hemodynamics, and their measurement may be useful in the assessment of cardiovascular risk in patients with hypertension.
the evaluation of central hemodynamic parameters and arterial stiffness is important to better understand the cardiovascular pathophysiology in hypertension.
